documents.title: Rust async tokio runtime
documents.content: Tokio is an async runtime for the Rust programming language, providing the building blocks for writing network applications. It offers a multi-threaded work-stealing scheduler and supports both TCP and UDP protocols.

documents.title: Meilisearch full-text search
documents.content: Meilisearch is a lightweight, fast, and open-source search engine that delivers instant and relevant search results out of the box. It uses BM25-like ranking and supports typo tolerance, filters, and faceting.

documents.title: Caching strategies in distributed systems
documents.content: Distributed caches reduce latency and backend load. Strategies include read-through, write-through, write-behind, and cache-aside. TTL and eviction policies determine freshness versus memory pressure.

documents.title: Vector databases for embeddings
documents.content: Vector databases like Qdrant, Pinecone, and Milvus store high-dimensional embeddings and enable similarity search using cosine distance, dot product, or Euclidean distance. They power modern RAG and recommendation systems.

documents.title: HTTP caching headers explained
documents.content: Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified, and Vary headers control how HTTP responses are cached by browsers and CDNs. Cache-Control: max-age=N sets freshness in seconds. Must-revalidate forces rechecking stale entries.

documents.title: Rust error handling with Result
documents.content: Rust uses Result<T, E> for recoverable errors and panic! for unrecoverable ones. The ? operator propagates errors up the call stack. anyhow::Result is a common choice for application code; thiserror for library code.

documents.title: PostgreSQL pgvector extension
documents.content: pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension for vector similarity search. It supports exact nearest neighbor search via ORDER BY embedding <-> query, and approximate search using ivfflat or hnsw indexes.

documents.title: gRPC and Protocol Buffers
documents.content: gRPC is a high-performance RPC framework that uses HTTP/2 for transport and Protocol Buffers for serialization. It supports streaming, deadlines, cancellation, and bidirectional communication.

documents.title: BM25 ranking algorithm
documents.content: BM25 (Best Matching 25) is a probabilistic ranking function used by search engines to score document relevance. It considers term frequency, document length, and inverse document frequency across a corpus.

documents.title: Docker multi-stage builds
documents.content: Multi-stage Docker builds use multiple FROM statements in a single Dockerfile to compile artifacts in one stage and copy only the necessary binaries to a smaller runtime image. This dramatically reduces final image size.
